gaps.sentence: He earns fifty thousand pounds ___ year.
gaps.explanation: 'Fifty thousand a year' — 'a' = per in rates.

gaps.sentence: These apples cost two euros ___ kilo.
gaps.explanation: 'A/per' is used for rates: two euros a kilo, twice a week, 60 km an hour.

gaps.sentence: He joined ___ army when he was eighteen.
gaps.explanation: Institutions take 'the': the army, the police, the church.

gaps.sentence: He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
gaps.explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: We stayed at ___ hotel right next to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'The station' — in a town there is usually one known station; context makes it definite.

gaps.sentence: My grandmother goes to ___ church every morning before work.
gaps.explanation: 'Go to church' (as worshipper) takes no article; 'the church' would mean the building.
'MA' is pronounced /em/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an MA'.

gaps.sentence: ___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.
